# rmux 0.1.9 — preview
This release polishes command search and keyboard focus in the app and browser demo.
## Command palette
- Search native workspaces by project path, group, or description, including workspaces in other windows. The current workspace is marked in results. - Workspace shortcut hints follow your configured bindings. - The browser palette follows the native command order, with New Workspace and New Tab near the top. Page navigation accounts for two-line workspace results. - Shell line-start, line-end, and delete-to-start actions share bindings and command names across the native app and demo.
## Keyboard focus
- Canceling the terminal tab chooser returns focus to where you opened it, including Find. Choosing a tab focuses that terminal. - Opening the chooser from its toolbar no longer steals focus before saving the return target.
## Availability
GitHub builds the signed and notarized macOS Apple Silicon DMG and ZIP, Linux x86-64 tarball, and Windows x86-64 ZIP. macOS updates use Sparkle. The [browser demo](https://rmux.app) uses bundled sample sessions, not real shells. The [VS Code guide](https://rmux.app/vscode/) explains how to open and reuse a project workspace with VS Code’s external-terminal command.
Focused compilation and browser interaction checks cover the polish changes. Native visual review and native Windows runtime validation remain pending. Per-terminal persistent shell history is still under development and is not enabled.
